The '''2024–25 season''' was the [[List of Chelsea F.C. seasons|119th season]] in the history of [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea Football Club]], and their 36th consecutive season in the top flight of [[Football in England|English football]]. In addition to the [[2024–25 Premier League|domestic league]], the club participated in the [[2024–25 FA Cup|FA Cup]] and the [[2024–25 EFL Cup|EFL Cup]]. In international football, Chelsea contested and won both the [[2024–25 UEFA Conference League|UEFA Conference League]] and the expanded [[2025 FIFA Club World Cup|FIFA Club World Cup]], with this season being their first participation in the former.

==Season summary==
On 3 June 2024, the club announced that [[Leicester City F.C.|Leicester City]] manager [[Enzo Maresca]] would be joining as head coach on 1 July 2024, signing a five-year deal with an option to extend for a further year.<ref name=Marescahire/>

Despite an opening day defeat to [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]], Chelsea would only lose one of their next sixteen games and looked to be unlikely title challengers to runaway leaders [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]]. On 11 October, Cole Palmer was named the [[Premier League Player of the Month]] for September,<ref name=PalmerPoM /> which largely owed to a spectacular performance where he scored four goals in the first half in a 4-2 victory over [[Brighton and Hove Albion F.C.|Brighton and Hove Albion]].<ref>https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/czeg10p13l9t</ref> Meanwhile,
Enzo Maresca picked up the [[Premier League Manager of the Month|Manager of the Month]] award.<ref name=MarescaMoM /> However, a poor run of form beginning with a Boxing Day defeat to local rivals [[Fulham F.C.|Fulham]] meant Chelsea's domestic campaign ultimately became a fight to finish in the Top 5 and secure a [[2025–26 UEFA Champions League|Champions League]] place.

[[File:Chelsea and Wolves teams line up 20 January 2025.jpg|thumb|right|Chelsea players lining up against [[Wolverhampton Wanderers F.C.|Wolverhampton Wanderers]] on 20 January 2025 at Stamford Bridge]]
On 30 April 2025, having played most of the season without a front of shirt, Chelsea announced a deal with Dubai-based property development firm [[DAMAC Properties|DAMAC]] to feature on the kit for the rest of the season in addition to a long-term club partnership.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.chelseafc.com/en/news/article/chelsea-partners-with-damac-properties|title=Chelsea partners with DAMAC Properties|website=Chelsea F.C.|date=30 April 2025|accessdate=29 May 2025}}</ref> 

On 25 May, Chelsea defeated [[Nottingham Forest F.C.|Nottingham Forest]] on the final match day of the Premier League season to finish fourth in the table, securing a place in the league phase of the [[2025–26 UEFA Champions League]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/c3v551xvrdkt|title=Levi Cowill seals Chelsea's Champions League place|website=BBC|date=25 May 2025|accessdate=29 May 2025}}</ref> This confirmed Chelsea's participation in the UEFA Champions League for the first time since the [[2022–23 UEFA Champions League]], and the first time that Chelsea had secured a place in European football's elite competition under new owners [[BlueCo]].<ref name=BlueCoWin />

On 28 May, Chelsea defeated [[Real Betis]] 4–1 in the [[2025 UEFA Conference League final|final]] of the UEFA Conference League.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/crk2zx2e1xet|title=Chelsea beat Real Betis 4-1 to win Conference League|website=BBC Sport|date=28 May 2025|access-date=28 May 2025}}</ref> In doing so, Chelsea became the first club to win each of the five major European competitions.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.chelseafc.com/en/news/article/chelsea-win-the-conference-league|title=Chelsea win the Conference League!|publisher=Chelsea F.C.|date=28 May 2025|access-date=28 May 2025}}</ref> Cole Palmer was named Man of the Match in the final after providing two assists.<ref name="MOTM">{{cite web |url=https://www.uefa.com/uefaconferenceleague/news/0299-1dde145a671c-b19ce043dde1-1000/ |title=Cole Palmer named official 2025 UEFA Conference League final Player of the Match |website=UEFA.com|publisher=Union of European Football Associations |date=28 May 2025 |access-date=28 May 2025}}</ref> He was also named in the team of the tournament along with teammates [[Filip Jörgensen]], [[Tosin Adarabioyo]], and [[Enzo Fernández]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefaconferenceleague/news/0299-1ddf88ed7508-8d7f67b21f73-1000--2024-25-uefa-conference-league-team-of-the-season/ |title=2024/25 UEFA Conference League Team of the Season |website=[[UEFA]] |publisher=Union of European Football Associations |date=29 May 2025 |access-date=29 May 2025}}</ref> The success marked the first silverware won in the BlueCo era.<ref name=BlueCoWin>{{cite web|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2025/may/28/pellegrini-betis-maresca-chelsea-conference-league-final-chess|title=Pellegrini and Betis familiar pawns in Maresca’s search for winning move|website=The Guardian|date=28 May 2025|accessdate=8 July 2025}}</ref>

On 8 July 2025, Chelsea secured a spot in the [[2025 FIFA Club World Cup final|final]] of the newly revamped [[FIFA Club World Cup]] with a 2–0 win over Brazilian side [[Fluminense FC|Fluminense]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=Steinberg |first=Jacob |date=2025-07-08 |title=João Pedro sends Chelsea to Club World Cup final as stunners sink Fluminense |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2025/jul/08/fluminense-chelsea-club-world-cup-semi-final-match-report |access-date=2025-07-08 |work=The Guardian |language=en-GB |issn=0261-3077}}</ref> Both goals were scored by new signing [[João Pedro (footballer, born 2001)|João Pedro]], who had only joined Chelsea from [[Brighton & Hove Albion F.C.|Brighton]] on 2 July and was making just his second appearance for the club.<ref>{{cite news |last=Collins |first=Ben |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/articles/cg75j2118e3o |title=Pedro joins Chelsea and could feature in Club World Cup |website=BBC Sport |date=2 July 2025 |access-date=2 July 2025}}</ref> On 13 July, Palmer scored twice and provided an assist for João Pedro in a 3–0 win over [[Paris Saint-Germain FC|Paris Saint-Germain]] in the final.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://news.sky.com/story/chelsea-win-fifa-club-world-cup-with-victory-over-psg-as-donald-trump-watches-from-stands-13396284 |title=Chelsea win FIFA Club World Cup with victory over PSG - as Donald Trump presents trophy |publisher=Sky News |date=13 July 2025 }}</ref> Palmer earned the [[FIFA Club World Cup awards#Golden Ball|Golden Ball]] award for his performance in the tournament and goalkeeper [[Robert Sánchez]] won the Golden Glove.<ref>{{cite web |last=Fentuo |first=Fentuo Tahiru |author-link=Fentuo Tahiru Fentuo |url=https://www.olympics.com/en/news/fifa-club-world-cup-2025-awards-cole-palmer-best-player-full-list |title=FIFA Club World Cup 2025 Awards: Cole Palmer named best player, Desire Doué wins best young player - full list |publisher=Olympics.com |date=14 July 2025 }}</ref>

==Pre-season and friendlies==
On 8 March, Chelsea announced a planned return to the [[United States]] during pre-season with matches later confirmed against [[Wrexham A.F.C.|Wrexham]], [[Club América]], [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]], [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]] and [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]].<ref>{{cite news|title=First two dates unveiled for USA 2024|url=https://www.chelseafc.com/en/news/article/first-two-dates-unveiled-for-usa-2024-club-chelsea-packages-on-sale|access-date=25 March 2024|publisher=Chelsea F.C.|date=8 March 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|title=United States date for Chelsea vs Celtic|url=https://www.chelseafc.com/en/news/article/united-states-date-for-chelsea-vs-celtic|access-date=25 March 2024|publisher=Chelsea F.C.|date=18 March 2024}}</ref> A sixth friendly was later announced, against [[Inter Milan]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Chelsea to host Italian champions Inter at Stamford Bridge|url=https://www.chelseafc.com/en/news/article/chelsea-to-host-italian-champions-inter-at-stamford-bridge|access-date=5 July 2024|publisher=Chelsea F.C.|date=5 July 2024}}</ref>

Chelsea entered the competition at the third round stage, and were drawn at home to [[Morecambe F.C.|Morecambe]].<ref>{{cite news|title=FA Cup third round proper draw|url=https://www.thefa.com/news/2024/dec/02/emirates-fa-cup-third-round-proper-draw-details-2024-25|access-date=2 December 2024|publisher=The Football Association|date=2 December 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|title=Morecambe FA Cup tie date and kick-off confirmed|url=https://www.chelseafc.com/en/news/article/morecambe-fa-cup-tie-date-and-kick-off-confirmed|access-date=9 December 2024|publisher=Chelsea FC|date=6 December 2024}}</ref> In the fourth round, they were drawn away to [[Brighton & Hove Albion F.C.|Brighton & Hove Albion]].<ref>{{cite news|title=The Emirates FA Cup fourth round proper draw has been confirmed|url=https://www.thefa.com/news/2025/jan/12/emirates-fa-cup-fourth-round-proper-draw-20251201|access-date=17 January 2025|publisher=The Football Association|date=12 January 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|title=Date confirmed for FA Cup trip to Brighton|url=https://www.chelseafc.com/en/news/article/date-confirmed-for-chelsea-brighton-fa-cup-tie|access-date=17 January 2025|publisher=Chelsea FC|date=17 January 2025}}</ref>

=====Quarter-finals=====
The draw for the order of the quarter-final legs was held on 21 February 2025, after the round of 16 draw. However, the order of legs in Chelsea's tie was later reversed in order to avoid a scheduling conflict with the [[2024–25 UEFA Europa League|Europa League]]'s [[2024–25 UEFA Europa League knockout phase#Tottenham Hotspur v Eintracht Frankfurt|Tottenham Hotspur v Eintracht Frankfurt match]] in the same city.<ref name="TOTUEL">{{cite news|last=Wakefield|first=Mark|url=https://www.football.london/chelsea-fc/news/uefa-make-huge-conference-league-31073706|title=UEFA make huge Conference League fixture announcement impacting Chelsea and Tottenham|work=Football London|date=24 February 2025|access-date=13 March 2025}}</ref>

===FIFA Club World Cup===
{{main|2025 FIFA Club World Cup}}
{{legend2|#CCFFCC|Win|border=1px solid #AAAAAA}}
{{legend2|#FFFFCC|Draw|border=1px solid #AAAAAA}}
{{legend2|#FFCCCC|Loss|border=1px solid #AAAAAA}}
{{legend2|#FFFFFF|Fixtures|border=1px solid #AAAAAA}}

====Group stage====
{{main|2025 FIFA Club World Cup Group D}}
The group stage draw was held on 5 December 2024. Chelsea were in Pot 2, being the 5th highest-ranked UEFA team in the competition.<ref>{{cite news|title=FIFA Club World Cup: Format, draw, teams, schedule ... Messi|url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/story/_/id/41959489/fifa-club-world-cup-format-schedule-why-lionel-messi-playing|access-date=5 December 2024|publisher=ESPN|date=5 December 2024}}</ref> They were drawn into Group D alongside [[2022 Copa Libertadores]] winners [[CR Flamengo|Flamengo]] and [[2023–24 CAF Champions League]] runners-up [[Espérance Sportive de Tunis|Espérance de Tunis]], from Brazil and Tunisia respectively.<ref>{{cite news|title=Club World Cup draw: Chelsea discover group stage opponents|url=https://www.chelseafc.com/en/news/article/club-world-cup-draw-chelsea-discover-group-stage-opponents|access-date=5 December 2024|publisher=Chelsea F.C.|date=5 December 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|title=Club World Cup: All you need to know as draw is made|url=https://www.premierleague.com/news/4184636|access-date=5 December 2024|publisher=Premier League|date=5 December 2024}}</ref> [[2023 CONCACAF Champions League]] winners [[Club León]] were removed from the tournament by FIFA on 21 March 2025. They were replaced by [[Los Angeles FC]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Club World Cup: Leon removed from competition over multi-club ownership|url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/story/_/id/44343954/club-world-cup-fifa-rules-leon-clears-pachuca|access-date=21 March 2025|publisher=ESPN}}</ref>
